page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 vCPUs powered by 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Hyperthreading provides two threads per physical core. The system includes 128 GB of RAM, offering a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. It operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. Local storage is not included, requiring external network-attached storage. No GPU accelerators are present.

In benchmark evaluations, single-threaded CPU metrics fall into the lower quartile, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 995.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1107.99. However, the 32 virtual cores allow multi-threaded performance to reach mid-range capabilities, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 23637.07 and a PassMark CPU score of 23223.67. Supported CPU instructions include AVX-512, AES encryption, and FMA, helping drive a PassMark CPU extended instructions test score of 24855.71 and memory read speeds up to 96.24 GB/s for large uncached blocks.

With its 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance provides cost efficiency for multi-core batch tasks, web server clusters, and middle-tier application deployments that rely on parallel execution rather than extreme per-core clock speed. The server delivers steady throughput for Redis operations at 22.63 million operations per second and static web serving at 17.15 GB/s. Primary tradeoffs involve lower single-thread execution speeds and the absence of direct attached NVMe local storage, making it best suited for scalable web serving, ETL pipelines, and enterprise software hosting supported by remote block storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.8xlarge is a general-purpose instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical Intel Xeon 8163 cores running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 128 GB of RAM and 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no local storage or GPUs. Hardware instruction sets include AVX-512, AES, and FMA. Benchmark data reflects weak single-threaded performance alongside average multi-core results, including a multi-core stress-ng score of 23637.07 and a PassMark CPU score of 23223.67. Memory bandwidth reaches 96.24 GB/s for uncached reads. The 1:4 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers quantitative resource balance for workloads prioritizing thread count over single-core speeds. It provides steady performance for Redis key-value caching, static web serving, and distributed batch processing, provided ephemeral local disk performance is not required.
